neighbours.label: the noun closing a fixed 'for ...' idiom of purpose or exclamation: 'for good measure', 'for fun', 'for heaven's sake'
fire: She added an extra lock to the door for good measure before leaving.
We tried the old recipe just for fun on Sunday afternoon.
Please, for heaven's sake, turn the music down a little.
He checked the tires twice more for good measure that morning.
The kids painted the fence purple purely for fun last summer.
Oh, for goodness' sake, just tell me the answer already.
They threw in a free dessert for good measure with the meal.
I learned to juggle simply for fun during the long winter.
quiet: She added an extra lock to the door as a safety step before leaving.
We tried the old recipe on Sunday afternoon with our cousins.
Please turn the music down a little, it is very late.
The new tax measure passed the city council that morning.
The kids painted the fence purple last summer with their father.
The council will measure the impact of the new road next year.
They threw in a free dessert with the meal at the end.
I learned to juggle during the long winter at my grandmother's house.

notes: Card top 32: ' fun' x11, ' good' x7, ' measure' x3, ' sake'. Near misses keep the sentence but drop the idiom, two use 'measure' outside the idiom. Opposite pole: 'for all I know' idiom.
